Synopsis:
Global equities and bonds rallied modestly while the yen surged toward its biggest two-day gain since August intervention. The pivot event is Friday's U.S. payrolls report following weak ADP data. Money markets price a ~60% probability of a Fed rate hike this month, up sharply from under 40% the prior week. Fed's Williams framed elevated long-term yields as a sign of economic strength rather than distress; Governor Waller is next to speak. U.S. 10-year yields pulled back slightly to 4.766% after recent multi-year highs. The dollar weakened, gold surged to $4,436/oz (+13% from June lows), oil dipped to ~$94.57/bbl despite renewed U.S.-Iran military exchange. The Dutch central bank relocated gold reserves from North America to London vaults.
